title: devbin conforms to the shared dev/opt/brew contract (docs/dev-opt-brew.md, vc decision 57): devbin use [dev|opt|brew], the machine pointer retired so the ~/.local/bin/devbin link read by path is the one record, the tree word in --version, install --force as the one re-publish route, T3's manifest keys
body:
On hv's ask of 2026-10-24, every tool released through Homebrew (Molt, Utilz, Intent and devbin) solves dev, opt and brew identically. The shared contract was agreed at v0.4 by all four projects' validation nodes (vc decision 57). It lands as `docs/dev-opt-brew.md`, and this issue is devbin's conformance to it. The contract's sections are cited as T1 to T10.

What devbin has today, measured at lib/helpers:3210-3480, lib/cmd/install and packaging/homebrew/devbin.rb:

- **No `use` verb.** The choice of install is a pointer FILE, `$XDG_DATA_HOME/devbin/home`. A publish writes it, or `install --point` and `upgrade --point` on a brew machine.
- **The chooser** (`machine_install_chooser`) reads `DEVBIN_INSTALL_PREFIX`, then the pointer, then `$HOMEBREW_PREFIX/opt/devbin/libexec`.
- **`--version`** prints the version and sha, then `install: <path>`, with no tree word.
- **A re-publish** is `bin/devbin upgrade` in devbin's own tree, and an existing prefix refuses `install`.
- **The manifest header** carries `kind`, `source`, `source_commit`, `devbin_version` and `managed_by`, not T3's `tool` and `version`.

The changes:

1. **`devbin use [dev|opt|brew]` (T5).** It manages one link, `~/.local/bin/devbin`.
   - `use dev` and `use opt` point the link at that tree's `bin/devbin`. dev is the checkout; opt is `install.prefix`.
   - `use brew` removes the link, so no link means brew.
   - A bare `use` reports and changes nothing.
   - Each refuses a missing tree, naming the step that makes it.
   - Doctor, and a bare `use`, fail when the link is not the first `devbin` on PATH, comparing resolved directories.
   - Nothing else (fleet, upgrade, install) points or removes the link.
   - A test-only option may name the link directory.
2. **The machine pointer is retired (T9).** The chooser becomes `DEVBIN_INSTALL_PREFIX`, then the tree that `~/.local/bin/devbin` resolves to, read by its path rather than through PATH, then `$HOMEBREW_PREFIX/opt/devbin/libexec`. A brew root is named by its opt link (`install_named_root`).
   - `install --point` and `upgrade --point` go.
   - A pointer file still on a machine is named by doctor as retired, with the remedy `devbin use opt` (or `use brew`), and is never read.
   - Every reader keeps one answer (Highlander): doctor, upgrade, vendor, the update notice, shell-init's `dvb` and fleet all ask the one chooser.
3. **One tree function and the version line (T4).** brew by `managed_by: brew`; opt by a manifest whose `tool` is devbin; dev by a git work tree with no install manifest; unknown otherwise. `devbin --version` and doctor print `devbin <version> (<tree>, <sha12>[+dirty]) at <absolute root>`. Every reader of the old two-line form moves with it, its tests included.
4. **Publish (T2).** `install --force` replaces an existing opt install whose manifest says devbin wrote it, and it is the one re-publish route. `upgrade` in devbin's own tree stops publishing and names `install --force`. The dirty refusal and `--managed-by brew` stay.
5. **The manifest (T3).** The install manifest's header gains `tool: devbin` and `version` beside devbin's own keys. An install in the older form is named with its remedy (`install --force` for opt, `brew upgrade devbin` for brew), and doctor fails until then. A vendored project's manifest is a project's record, not a tree's, and is unchanged.
6. **Docs.** The README's maintainer section, `lib/pages/install.md`, `upgrade.md`, `shell-init.md` and `doctor.md`, and the formula's caveats name `devbin use` in place of the pointer and `--point`.

Done when:
- `devbin use` exists as T5 says, and the shadow check holds.
- No code reads or writes the machine pointer except doctor naming a leftover one.
- The chooser reads the link by path.
- `--version` prints T4's line.
- `install --force` is the one re-publish route.
- The install manifest carries T3's keys, and an older form is named with its remedy.
- T10's proof: `bin/devbin doctor` names the install the switch chose, for each of dev, opt and brew, in checkouts of Molt, Utilz, Intent (through intent-vc, Intent's upgrade only in a scratch clone after its v3.2.6 tag) and devbin, booked through molt-vc.
- It ships in the release before devbin's public push.

## Resolution

Fixed at 76b3d790 and shipped in devbin 0.1.14, the release before devbin's public one (decisions 60 and 61). It landed on landing suite 20261024-1122 at 584c6ba0, where every test passed or skipped for its environment and the errors seal was empty (kept at ~/Devel/scratch/devbin-vc/clone-archive/seals/land213-20261024-1122). cc built it in a scratch clone of main, and vc landed it.

- **`devbin use [dev|opt|brew]`** (T5): one link, `~/.local/bin/devbin`.
  - `use dev` and `use opt` point it, from the dev checkout only, and are refused elsewhere naming the command.
  - `use brew` removes a link into devbin's trees and nothing else, so no link means brew; a bare `use` reports.
  - The shadow check (`devbin_link_shadow`) is shared with doctor and compares resolved directories.
  - No other verb writes the link.
  - **A project does not offer it** (decision 59). A project with devbin vendored into it refuses `use` with exit 6, naming `devbin use`, and its help leaves the command out. One predicate, `devbin_tree_refusal`, answers for the dispatcher, `command_active` and help. A project with a `use` command of its own runs that.
- **The machine pointer is retired** (T9). The chooser reads `DEVBIN_INSTALL_PREFIX`, else the link by its own path, else Homebrew's opt link.
  - The pointer's writer, `point_refusal`, `is_install_prefix` and `--point` are gone.
  - Doctor names a pointer file still on disk as a note, and nothing reads it.
  - Routing follows the switch for every recorded kind. Under `use dev` a project records `checkout`, with `+dirty` when the tree is dirty.
  - `DEVBIN_SOURCE` is `dvb`'s fallback alone: nothing in the runtime or the suite places a source through it.
- **The tree line** (T4): `devbin_tree` and `devbin_tree_line`, printed by `--version` and `version` from an install and from devbin's checkout. A consumer keeps its own line. An unreadable checkout reads `(dev, unknown)`, and doctor's tree row fails on it.
- **`install --force` is the one re-publish route** (T2), and `upgrade` in the checkout names it.
  - Issue 0146's behaviour (warn, then replace an opt install that has no manifest) is WITHDRAWN by the contract (T2, decision 58). Such a prefix is refused, naming its remedy: move it aside, then `install`.
  - A manifest with no rows (issue 0159) still says devbin wrote it, and is still replaced unchecked.
  - An unreadable manifest is named first (issue 0144).
- **The install manifest carries T3's keys**: `tool: devbin`, `version`, and `managed_by` always.
  - An old opt install fails doctor naming `install --force`.
  - An old keg, or a keg with no manifest under the opt link, is `brew`, and doctor notes it, naming `brew upgrade devbin` (T3 as amended, decision 58).
- **The suite's HOME is the test's own**, with its `~/.local/bin` first on PATH. One run of every file that reads HOME, green before any 0213 code, measured that, so no link-dir variable entered the product.

### T10's proof

Each run below was judged in a fresh login shell's PATH, and each passed.

- **rhadamanth: devbin's checkout, and scratch clones of Molt and Utilz vendored from main, 2026-10-24 11:43Z to 11:45Z (cc, in one machine-change slot booked with molt-vc, decision 61).**
  - `bin/devbin install --force` republished opt in the new manifest form.
  - Under each of `use dev`, `use opt` and `use brew`, `devbin --version` and a bare `devbin use` named the install the switch chose. In the checkout and in each clone, `doctor` failed no check, and its switch row named that install. `vendor` compared each clone against it.
  - Under brew, the 0.1.13 keg, which predates 0213, printed the old version line and had no `use`, and doctor noted its manifest form, naming `brew upgrade devbin`.
  - The first try at `use dev` was judged in the agent session's own PATH, which still put Homebrew's bin ahead of `~/.local/bin`. doctor's switch row failed there on the shadow, naming the PATH fix, as T5 asks.
  - The machine was left on brew, with no link.
  - Outputs: `~/Devel/scratch/devbin-cc/t10/out/0-baseline.txt` to `6-brew.txt`.
- **rhadamanth: an Intent scratch clone at 141dcf9ff, 2026-10-25 05:11Z to 05:12Z (cc), with devbin at 0.1.14.**
  - `install --force` republished opt at 07f625a8.
  - Under each of dev, opt and brew, `use` and `--version` named the switch's install. Under brew that was the keg's T4 line, `devbin 0.1.14 (brew, 593109bfb124) at /opt/homebrew/opt/devbin/libexec`.
  - `doctor` failed no check and named that install, and `vendor` read it.
  - Under dev and opt, doctor's source row said the devbin the clone came from had moved on, when it had moved only outside the vendored files. That is issue 0224, fixed in 0.1.15.
  - Outputs: `c1-install-force.txt` to `c4-brew.txt` in the same directory.
- **kovacs, Ubuntu ARM64 with brew alone, 2026-10-26 08:04Z (cc's legd.sh, sha256 88796665, run by kovacs-sysadm in devbin's kovacs slot).**
  - Against the 0.1.14 keg, with no `~/.local/bin/devbin` and only Homebrew's `devbin` on PATH.
  - A bare `devbin use` exited 0, printing `use: no link, so brew` and `  devbin 0.1.14 (brew, 593109bfb124) at /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/opt/devbin/libexec`.
  - A vendored fixture's `bin/devbin doctor` printed `  ok    switch: no link, so brew`, failed no check and exited 0.
  - legd.rc was 0. The logs are on kovacs: `~/work/devbin-cc/legd.log`, `legd-use.out` and `legd-doctor.out`.
